title: C# OOP versus JavaScript and TypeScript
hook: TypeScript looks like C# in a slide deck. The CLR keeps types, accessibility, and virtual slots at run time. The TS compiler erases them. Interviews fail when you describe C# as “TS with a runtime.”

sections.heading: Nominal metadata versus structural erase
sections.prose: A C# class, interface, or record is a named CLR type. Casts and is/as check that type. A TypeScript interface is a compile-time shape; two different interface names with the same fields are interchangeable, and they vanish in the JS output. C# privacy (module 04) is enforced by the runtime: reflection can still skip it if you ask, but ordinary IL cannot read a private field from another type. TS private is a compiler error; JS #fields are a different, weaker analogue.

sections.heading: Dispatch, identity, and values
sections.prose: C# virtual dispatch uses a method table. JS looks up a property on the prototype chain, which you can mutate at runtime. C# structs are real value types; TS object types are never copied as values. Records give you generated value equality; JS still needs a library or JSON.stringify hacks. None of this makes C# “better” — it makes the answers different when you debug a Redis DTO that looked equal in JSON but missed a Dictionary lookup.

snippets.label: TS structural typing that C# would reject
snippets.explanation: TypeScript allows the assignment. In C#, AuthHint and CacheEntry as distinct classes or interfaces are not assignable without a relationship. That is nominal typing backed by metadata.

sections.heading: What to say in a mixed-stack interview
sections.prose: You ship both: a .NET worker and a TS client. Say: the client’s types are documentation the bundler deletes; the worker’s types are the CLR’s. Auth tokens validated on the server are records or classes with private key material. The browser object that holds the same JWT is a string plus a parsed JSON object with no access modifiers. Polymorphism on the server is virtual or interface dispatch; on the client it is functions on objects.

interviewTakeaways: C# accessibility and interfaces survive as metadata; TS types erase.
C# is nominally typed at runtime; TS is structural at compile time.
Value types and virtual slots have no honest JS equivalent.
commonPitfalls: Calling TS private “the same as C# private.”
Assuming a TS interface will exist in a stack trace.

jsTsCorrelations.note: tsc strips types. The CLR loads them. This is the whole page in one sentence.
JS has objects, prototypes, and modules. No IL, no method table you control with virtual, no private metadata.
